withdraw.missing: A road-user class that decides membership of 'an authorized emergency vehicle' (DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle: 'a vehicle permitted to depart from certain traffic laws when equipped and operated in the manner provided by law'). The run's reading admits this aggregate but classifies every road-user class under it as unresolved, ru.emergency_vehicle, ru.fire_apparatus and ru.motor_vehicle included, and none as included. Under ru.aggregate membership is then never true, and it is unknown for every vehicle. The siren duty (s3) and its exception (s4, s5) are therefore never decided for any road user. No faithful record can reach a violated or compliant verdict, and a private car is never decidedly outside the subject class. The span needs either an observable class that carries the authorization (a vehicle bearing the designation and equipment of an authorized emergency vehicle) or the reading's classification of the definition's members, for example ru.emergency_vehicle and ru.fire_apparatus as included and ru.motor_vehicle as covered or excluded. This decides the road users the duty concerns: which vehicles may not use a siren except in response or pursuit.
nearest: ru.aggregate: 'true when the user carries an included class, unknown when no included class holds and the user carries an unresolved class ...; a covered or excluded class decides nothing', and 'an admitted aggregate stays an aggregate even when it contains only one class'. The admitted aggregate must be claimed as the aggregate, and with no included class it can never hold.

ru.emergency_vehicle: 'vehicle of a class the jurisdiction designates as emergency'. It is not claimable for s1, because 'Not a stand-in for: a named road-user class ...' on ru.aggregate leaves the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-020::authorized_emergency_vehicle to carry 'authorized emergency vehicle', and the run classifies ru.emergency_vehicle under it as unresolved.
